title: Arcade Token Change
statement: An arcade's token machine uses coin values that change by country, such as [1, 7, 10]. For any amount up to 50,000 it must pay out the fewest coins.

approaches.name: DP over amounts: best(a) = 1 + min best(a − coin)
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: Exact for every coin system and fast enough: 500,000 steps.

approaches.name: BFS from 0, adding one coin per level
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Same bound; each level is one more coin.

approaches.name: Always pay the largest coin that fits
approaches.label: unsuitable

approaches.name: Plain recursion over the last coin without storing results
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: Solves the same amounts again and again.

title: Warehouse Robot Routes
statement: A warehouse floor is a 200 × 200 grid with some shelves blocking cells. A robot moves only right or down from the loading dock (top-left) to the shipping door (bottom-right). The planner needs the number of routes modulo 1,000,000,007.

approaches.name: Grid DP: routes(r, c) = routes from above + routes from the left
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: 40,000 cells, each filled once from two neighbours.

approaches.name: Recursion with memoization from the door back to the dock
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Same work; deep recursion may need care.

approaches.name: Walk every route with DFS and count
approaches.label: unsuitable

approaches.name: Use the binomial formula C(r + c, r)
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: Only correct when no cell is blocked.

title: Document Diff Tool
statement: A writing app compares two drafts of up to 3,000 words each and must report the longest sequence of words that appears in both drafts in the same order, to highlight what was kept.
examples: "the cat sat" vs "the dog sat" → "the sat" (2 words)

approaches.name: 2-D DP: lcs(i, j) from lcs(i − 1, j − 1) + 1 on a match, else the larger of lcs(i − 1, j) and lcs(i, j − 1)
approaches.label: best
approaches.space: O(n · m), or O(m) for the length only
approaches.why: 9 million cells is fine, and the table can be walked back to show the kept words.

approaches.name: Walk both drafts and match each word with its next occurrence
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: An early match can skip a much longer common run later.

approaches.name: Try every subsequence of one draft and check it in the other
approaches.label: unsuitable

approaches.name: Recursion on (i, j) with memoization
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Same table filled lazily; recursion depth up to 6,000 needs care.
